description.summary: whose menus belong to which window

protocol.description:
A global menu bar has to show the menus of the application whose window is focused, and only the compositor knows which surface that is. An application therefore tells the compositor, per surface, where its menus are published; the compositor tells the menu bar — and nobody else — where the focused surface's menus are whenever focus moves.
The address is bound to a surface, by the client that owns the surface, on the connection that proves it. Nothing here trusts an app_id.

description.summary: publish where a surface's menus live
destroy the manager; addresses already set remain

request.name: set_address

description.summary: this surface's menus are published at this address

request.description: Set or replace the menu address of a surface this client owns. An empty address withdraws it. The address is a CurrentIPC service name (MenuWire, PHASE10 P10.2). It is forgotten when the surface is destroyed.

interface.name: abyss_menubar_v1

description.summary: the menu bar's view of focus

interface.description: Offered only to clients that connected to the compositor's privileged socket (PHASE10 §6.1). It says which application is frontmost and where its menus are, which is exactly what an ordinary client must not learn.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: the focused window publishes no menus, or nothing is focused

entry.name: gtk
entry.summary: a GTK application's bus name and menu paths (P10.6)

event.name: focused

description.summary: focus moved; here is where its menus are

event.description: Sent once on bind, and again whenever keyboard focus moves to a different toplevel, or the focused toplevel's address changes. With kind none, address is empty.

request.name: force_quit

description.summary: end an application that has stopped responding

request.description: Kill every client with a toplevel of this app_id. Only the compositor knows which processes those are, and only the menu bar — on the privileged socket — may ask (PHASE10 P10.8). The compositor never kills itself.
